stories.title: TB 26-10 Printed Circuit Board Assembly Chip Resistor Body Cracking
stories.summary: NASA identified factors contributing to rare chip resistor cracking on printed circuit boards during thermal cycling after vibration, including component orientation, excessive solder, and mounting stresses. Recommendations include careful component placement, finite element analysis, controlled solder fillet height, and functional thermal shock testing to mitigate flexure-induced cracking risks in ceramic body components.
stories.finding: NASA identified factors contributing to rare chip resistor cracking on printed circuit boards during thermal cycling after vibration, including component orientation, excessive solder, and mounting stresses. Recommendations include careful component placement, finite element analysis, controlled solder fillet height, and functional thermal shock testing to mitigate flexure-induced cracking risks in ceramic body components.
stories.significance: This finding is significant for NASA projects that widely use chip resistors, as it provides insights into potential failure mechanisms and offers guidelines to mitigate flexure-induced cracking risks in ceramic body components on printed circuit boards, thereby enhancing reliability and safety of electronic systems.
stories.caveat: The source does not specify material limitations; independent verification is not established.

inputFacts.title: TB 26-10 Printed Circuit Board Assembly Chip Resistor Body Cracking
inputFacts.summary: Two instances of thick-film chip resistor cracking were observed during thermal cycling after vibration testing on printed circuit board assemblies, with fractures occurring across the short axis due to bending. Failure analyses ruled out defective lots and fatigue, identifying board flexure, component orientation, excessive solder, and mounting stresses as contributing factors.
inputFacts.finding: Two instances of thick-film chip resistor cracking were observed during thermal cycling after vibration testing on printed circuit board assemblies, with fractures occurring across the short axis due to bending. Failure analyses ruled out defective lots and fatigue, identifying board flexure, component orientation, excessive solder, and mounting stresses as contributing factors.

editorial.reason: This article presents a new finding regarding a specific failure mode in electronic components, which is relevant to engineering and technology. The findings are substantive and offer practical mitigation strategies.
editorial.groundingReason: The article details NASA's identification of factors contributing to rare chip resistor cracking and provides specific recommendations to mitigate these risks, representing a new finding and technical advance in component reliability for NASA projects.

stories.title: NASA-funded Study Details One of Oldest Mars Meteorites Ever Found
stories.summary: Scientists have age-dated the Martian meteorite Teghaza 001 to over 4.1 billion years old, making it one of the most ancient found on Earth. Its unique mix of igneous minerals provides a rare snapshot of Mars' early crust formation and suggests a dynamic water cycle on the planet around that time.
stories.finding: Scientists have age-dated the Martian meteorite Teghaza 001 to over 4.1 billion years old, making it one of the most ancient found on Earth. Its unique mix of igneous minerals provides a rare snapshot of Mars' early crust formation and suggests a dynamic water cycle on the planet around that time.
stories.significance: As one of the oldest Martian meteorites discovered, Teghaza 001 provides a rare, early-history sample of the Martian crust, offering insights into the planet's geological formation and its ancient interaction with water.
stories.caveat: The exact origin of the meteorite on Mars remains unknown, and the study relies on mineralogical and chemical comparisons to potential source locations rather than direct sampling.

stories.title: New dwarf planet candidate discovered by NSF–DOE Rubin Observatory
stories.summary: Scientists using the NSF–DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory have identified a large object, provisionally designated ED138, orbiting beyond Pluto. Preliminary analysis suggests it may be one of the largest dwarf planet candidates ever found, potentially joining the five known dwarf planets if confirmed by follow-up observations.
stories.finding: Scientists using the NSF–DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory have identified a large object, provisionally designated ED138, orbiting beyond Pluto. Preliminary analysis suggests it may be one of the largest dwarf planet candidates ever found, potentially joining the five known dwarf planets if confirmed by follow-up observations.
stories.significance: If confirmed, ED138 would join the five other known dwarf planets, expanding our understanding of the solar system's composition and the objects residing in its distant regions. The discovery highlights the Rubin Observatory's capability to detect moving objects in crowded star fields.
stories.caveat: The object ED138 is currently a "dwarf planet candidate" and its classification is preliminary. Further observations by other observatories are needed to confirm its nature and status as a dwarf planet.

stories.title: NASA’s Perseverance Offers Clues to Protect Crews From Mars Dust
stories.summary: NASA's Perseverance rover measured fine and ultrafine Martian dust particles clinging to spacesuit materials over 1,645 Martian days. The findings, to be published in PNAS, indicate these particles are small enough to penetrate lungs and bloodstream, informing future spacesuit and habitat designs, dust-removal procedures, and crew health standards for Mars missions.

The findings, to be published in PNAS, indicate these particles are small enough to penetrate lungs and bloodstream, informing future spacesuit and habitat designs, dust-removal procedures, and crew health standards for Mars missions.
stories.significance: These measurements provide data to inform the design of future spacesuits, habitats, and dust-mitigation procedures, as fine particles can potentially penetrate human lungs and enter the bloodstream.
stories.caveat: The health risks of Mars dust are believed to depend on the quantity of dust and length of exposure, but specific human health impacts from these specific particle sizes on Mars remain to be determined.

inputFacts.summary: In Nigeria, exposure to high wet-bulb globe temperatures is associated with an increased likelihood of early pregnancy termination and a shift in the timing of conceptions, where initial declines in conception rates are followed by increases in subsequent months.

inputFacts.title: Chimpanzees at war: U-M researcher finds hope for humanity
inputFacts.summary: A long-term study of Ngogo chimpanzees in Kibale National Park, Uganda, observed a large community of nearly 200 individuals split into two groups, leading to lethal intergroup aggression resulting in 28 deaths over nine years. This aggression occurred between individuals who had previously coexisted, affiliated, and cooperated.

inputFacts.title: Stars brewing in a nebulous cauldron
inputFacts.summary: Astronomers detected extremely dim stars less than a tenth as massive as the Sun and distinguished larger, hotter, fully evolved stars from young stellar objects still wrapped in thick clouds within the N159 star-forming region in the Large Magellanic Cloud. Their results indicate that the western region of N159 has a higher concentration of young stellar objects, suggesting it is in an earlier stage of stellar collapse.

inputFacts.summary: Researchers at the University of Michigan Engineering, University of Illinois, and BAE Systems propose that more efficient software design could reduce AI energy consumption by up to half. inputFacts.summary: The Cassini spacecraft captured an image of plumes continuously spewing into space from the south pole of Saturn's moon Enceladus, backlit by the Sun. inputFacts.title: Cyprus: Island of Snakes, Cats, and Ophiolites
inputFacts.summary: The Akrotiri Peninsula on Cyprus formed from two land bridges, or tombolos, created by river and marine sediments. The more westerly Kouris River tombolo developed approximately 50,000 years ago, while the eastern tombolo, which cut off the Mediterranean Sea to form Akrotiri Salt Lake, formed within the past 2,000 years.

inputFacts.summary: Five University of Michigan researchers were elected as fellows of the American Physical Society for their contributions to physics, chemistry, nuclear engineering, and aerospace engineering. inputFacts.title: Michigan Minds: The rural healthcare blame game
inputFacts.summary: Rural white voters often perceive healthcare access and policy through a racialized "us-vs.-them" lens, believing that certain health policies disproportionately benefit racial and ethnic minority groups over rural white communities, even when objective data does not support this view. This perception is influenced by political rhetoric and media framing that connect health issues with racial considerations.
